requirements.requirement: AIDE (or equivalent tool) installed and configured to monitor /etc with content-level integrity checks
requirements.summary: aide/aide-common installed via apt; packaged aide.conf.d rules confirmed to apply a recursive '/ Full' catch-all rule (SHA256/SHA512/RMD160/TIGER/HAVAL/GOST/CRC32 + metadata) covering /etc, with only narrow pre-existing exceptions (resolv.conf, adjtime) for known-volatile files. This is a reasonable, complete implementation choice for the stated goal.

requirements.requirement: Baseline database initialized and installed as the active database
requirements.summary: aideinit produced /var/lib/aide/aide.db with 70,149 entries; aide.db and aide.db.new confirmed to have identical md5sums, showing the freshly generated baseline is the active database at the configured path.

requirements.requirement: Baseline accurately reflects a clean /etc state (no spurious /etc entries)
requirements.summary: An immediate aide.wrapper --check after init showed differences only in ephemeral /run and lxcfs pseudo-files created by the exec session itself; grep -c "/etc/" against the log returned 0, confirming no false positives under /etc.

requirements.requirement: Baseline detects and reports later changes to files in /etc (core requirement)
requirements.summary: Appended a marker line to /etc/hosts and ran aide.wrapper --check; AIDE reported /etc/hosts changed with full before/after size, mtime, ctime, and all seven configured checksum values, directly demonstrating end-to-end detection and reporting of an /etc modification.

requirements.requirement: An ongoing/automated mechanism exists so future changes continue to be reported without manual intervention
requirements.summary: /etc/cron.daily/aide (from aide-common) is present and executable, and cron.service is enabled, providing automatic daily checks and reporting going forward.

requirements.requirement: System restored to a clean baseline state after the detection demonstration
requirements.summary: /etc/hosts was restored from the pre-tamper backup and aideinit was re-run, rebuilding the active database (new md5sum) to reflect the clean, restored /etc content.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) node1 restart evidence: pre-restart healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (a1dc8e25...) and a clean-under-/etc AIDE check were captured; a backgrounded reboot returned acknowledgement before disconnect; polling confirmed the node went down and came back; post-restart boot_id (2e616fe5...) differed, matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots exactly. Post-restart the AIDE database file was confirmed byte-identical (same md5) and a fresh check showed the only /etc/-matching lines were /var/spool/postfix/etc chroot copies (refreshed by postfix on boot), not real /etc files, with zero genuine /etc differences.

overall_summary: The executor established a fully functional AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1: the packaged AIDE config was verified to apply recursive full-content checksums to /etc, a baseline database was initialized and confirmed active, a live tamper-and-detect test on /etc/hosts proved end-to-end change detection and detailed reporting, the system was cleanly restored and re-baselined afterward, and the distro's daily cron job provides ongoing automated reporting. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol was executed completely and consistently, with boot-identity change corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots and post-restart recovery of the AIDE database and clean /etc state confirmed.
limitations: A single minor residual file (/tmp/postcheck.log) from the post-restart check was left on the node and not cleaned up; low impact given its non-sensitive content.

Post-restart AIDE checks show ongoing noise from /var/spool/postfix/etc chroot copies (refreshed on every boot) because they fall under the packaged '/ Full' rule without a dedicated VarDir/VarFile exception; this is a pre-existing characteristic of the default Debian/Ubuntu AIDE config rather than an executor-introduced defect, but it means future daily reports will include non-actionable postfix chroot entries alongside genuine /etc changes.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological command trace for state-changing actions. Package install (cmd-41d6d76fa7d8426d) and both aideinit runs (cmd-3c94e2193a9841dc, cmd-3c71897e4f774acb) are necessary prerequisites/final-state actions. The /etc/hosts tamper (cmd-3c317f96b3e8406e) was a bounded, low-risk mutation made solely to prove detection and was fully restored immediately after (cmd-5ce518d0f9ed467f), with the baseline re-initialized afterward (cmd-3c71897e4f774acb) — appropriately handled. The mandated reboot (cmd-de91e5966a474d8c) is outside the public task contract but required by the separate node-restart protocol; it was not gratuitous. One minor residue: /tmp/postcheck.log, created during the post-restart check (cmd-6c1acf43ce284a69), was left behind and is visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot — a small, non-sensitive, unremoved artifact rather than a security or stability concern. No failed services, no package inconsistency, and no listening-socket or exposure changes appear between before-prepare and after-executor snapshots.
